the-council-members-olaf-the-bard.speaker: Olaf the Bard
the-council-members-olaf-the-bard.text: Hello? Yes? You want something, outerlander?

the-council-members-olaf-the-bard.player: Are you a member of the council?

the-council-members-olaf-the-bard.speaker: Olaf the Bard
the-council-members-olaf-the-bard.text: Why, indeed I am, outerlander! My talents as an exemplary musician made it difficult for them not to accept me! Why do you wish to know this?

the-council-members-olaf-the-bard.player: Well, I ask because I am currently doing the Fremennik trials so as to join your clan. I need seven of the twelve council of elders to vote for me.

the-council-members-olaf-the-bard.speaker: Olaf the Bard
the-council-members-olaf-the-bard.text: Ahhh... and you wish to earn my vote? I will gladly accept you as a Fremennik should you be able to prove yourself to have a little musical ability!

the-council-members-olaf-the-bard.player: So how would I do that?

the-council-members-olaf-the-bard.speaker: Olaf the Bard
the-council-members-olaf-the-bard.text: Why, by playing in our longhall! All you need to do is impress the revellers there with a few verses of an epic of your own creation!

the-council-members-olaf-the-bard.speaker: Olaf the Bard
the-council-members-olaf-the-bard.text: So what say you outerlander? Are you up for the challenge?

steps.player: Sure! This certainly sounds pretty easy to accomplish - I'll have your vote in no time!

steps.speaker: Olaf the Bard
steps.text: That is great news outerlander! We always need more music lovers here!

the-council-members-olaf-the-bard-talkin.player: So how would I go about writing this epic?

the-council-members-olaf-the-bard-talkin.speaker: Olaf the Bard
the-council-members-olaf-the-bard-talkin.text: Well, first of all you are going to need an instrument. Like all true bards you are going to have to make this yourself.

the-council-members-olaf-the-bard-talkin.player: How do I make an instrument?

the-council-members-olaf-the-bard-talkin.speaker: Olaf the Bard
the-council-members-olaf-the-bard-talkin.text: Well, it is a long and drawn-out process. Just east of this village there is an unusually musical tree that can be used to make very high quality instruments.

the-council-members-olaf-the-bard-talkin.speaker: Olaf the Bard
the-council-members-olaf-the-bard-talkin.text: Cut a piece from it, and then carve it into a special shape that will allow you to string it. Using a knife as you would craft any other wooden object would be best for this.

the-council-members-olaf-the-bard-talkin.player: Then what do I need to do?

the-council-members-olaf-the-bard-talkin.speaker: Olaf the Bard
the-council-members-olaf-the-bard-talkin.text: Next you will need to string your lyre. There is a troll to the South-east who has some golden wool. I would not recommend using anything else to string your lyre with.

the-council-members-olaf-the-bard-talkin.player: Anything else?

the-council-members-olaf-the-bard-talkin.speaker: Olaf the Bard
the-council-members-olaf-the-bard-talkin.text: Well, when you have crafted your lyre you will need the blessing of the Fossegrimen to tune your lyre to perfection before you even consider a public performance.

the-council-members-olaf-the-bard-talkin.player: Who or what is Fossegrimen?

the-council-members-olaf-the-bard-talkin.speaker: Olaf the Bard
the-council-members-olaf-the-bard-talkin.text: Fossegrimen is a lake spirit that lives just a little way South-west of this village. Make her an offering of fish, and you will then be ready for your performance.

the-council-members-olaf-the-bard-talkin.speaker: Olaf the Bard
the-council-members-olaf-the-bard-talkin.text: Make sure you give her a suitable offering however. If the offering is found to be unworthy, then you may find yourself unable to play your lyre with any skill at all!

the-council-members-olaf-the-bard-talkin.player: So what would be a worthy offering?

the-council-members-olaf-the-bard-talkin.speaker: Olaf the Bard
the-council-members-olaf-the-bard-talkin.text: A raw shark, manta ray, or sea turtle should be sufficient as an offering.

the-council-members-olaf-the-bard-talkin.player: Okay, what else do I need to do?

the-council-members-olaf-the-bard-talkin.speaker: Olaf the Bard
the-council-members-olaf-the-bard-talkin.text: When you have crafted your lyre and been blessed by Fossegrimen, then you will finally be ready to make your performance to the revellers at the longhall.

the-council-members-olaf-the-bard-talkin.speaker: Olaf the Bard
the-council-members-olaf-the-bard-talkin.text: Head past the bouncers and onto the stage, and then begin to play. If all goes well, you should find the music spring to your mind and sing your own epic on the spot.

the-council-members-olaf-the-bard-talkin.speaker: Olaf the Bard
the-council-members-olaf-the-bard-talkin.text: I will observe both you and the audience, and if you show enough talent, I will happily vote in your favour at the council of elders.

the-council-members-olaf-the-bard-talkin.speaker: Olaf the Bard
the-council-members-olaf-the-bard-talkin.text: Is that clear enough, outerlander? Would you like me to repeat anything?

steps.text: It stalks the coastlines, invisible to all. It brings us bad fortunes, and curses our journeys across the seas. It is also unkillable by normal means.

steps.speaker: Sigli the Huntsman
steps.text: Well outerlander, should you accept my challenge I will show you a special hunter's trick that will help you. Do you accept the challenge?

steps.player: Well, I need every vote I can get in the council of elders, but this certainly sounds impossible to do...

steps.speaker: Sigli the Huntsman
steps.text: Not at all outerlander. The Draugen is indeed impossible to kill, but that is not the same as being impossible to fight against.

steps.speaker: Sigli the Huntsman
steps.text: Every time he takes a Fremennik life, he gains in power, so to keep it from becoming too powerful we hunters hunt it and steal its life force.
If the player does not have inventory space:

steps.speaker: Sigli the Huntsman
steps.text: To defeat the Draugen you will need a special item; I have one to give you but it seems as though your inventory is too full to accept it.
If the player has inventory space:

steps.speaker: Sigli the Huntsman
steps.text: We do this with a special talisman. Here, take it; it will let you track the Draugen while it's invisible, and when you defeat it will absorb its essence.
a Hunters' talisman

steps.speaker: Sigli the Huntsman
steps.text: I want you to track the Draugen, defeat it, and store its essence in that talisman for me. If you can do this important task for my clan, I will vote for you.

steps.speaker: Sigli the Huntsman
steps.text: Take care of the talisman, and see me when you have completed this task.

the-council-members-sigli-the-huntsman-t.speaker: Sigli the Huntsman
the-council-members-sigli-the-huntsman-t.text: Hello again outerlander. Have you managed to hunt down the terrible Draugen yet?
If the player has the talisman:

steps.player: Not yet...

steps.speaker: Sigli the Huntsman
steps.text: Hmmm. Laziness is not a trait that I admire. I suggest you go and do so if you wish me to vouchsafe for you to our council of elders.

the-council-members-sigli-the-huntsman-t.text: If the player does not have a talisman:

steps.player: Not yet... I lost the talisman you gave me.

steps.speaker: Sigli the Huntsman
steps.text: The typical careless regard for valuable objects I would expect from an outerlander such as yourself. Do not lose THIS one.
another Hunters' talisman

the-council-members-sigli-the-huntsman-u.text: If the player is north/south/west/east of the Draugen:

steps.text: The talisman guides you [south/north/east/west].

the-council-members-sigli-the-huntsman-u.text: If the player is south-west/south-east of the Draugen:

steps.text: The talisman guides you [north-east/north-west].

the-council-members-sigli-the-huntsman-u.text: If the player is north-east/north-west of the Draugen:

steps.text: The talisman guides you [south-west/south-east].

the-council-members-sigli-the-huntsman-u.text: If the Draugen moves whilst locating with the talisman:

steps.text: The Draugen has moved elsewhere...

the-council-members-sigli-the-huntsman-u.text: If the player is 3 tiles near the Draugen:

steps.text: The Draugen is here! Beware!
The player engages in combat with the Draugen.
You absorb the Draugen's essence into your talisman.

the-council-members-sigli-the-huntsman-u.text: If the player uses the locate feature on the talisman after the Draugan's defeat:

steps.text: You have already captured the Draugen.

the-council-members-sigli-the-huntsman-t.speaker: Sigli the Huntsman
the-council-members-sigli-the-huntsman-t.text: I saw the entire hunt. Let me take that talisman from you; I would be honoured to speak out for you to our council of elders after such a hunt, outerlander.

the-council-members-sigli-the-huntsman-t.speaker: Sigli the Huntsman
the-council-members-sigli-the-huntsman-t.text: Absolutely outerlander! Anyone brave enough to hunt and defeat the Draugen will be a great addition to our clan!

the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.player: Are you a member of the council?

the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.speaker: Sigmund The Merchant
the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.text: That I am outerlander; it is a position that brings my family and I pride.

the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.player: I was wondering if I can count on your vote at the council of elders?

the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.speaker: Sigmund The Merchant
the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.text: You wish to become a Fremennik? I may be persuaded to swing my vote to your favour, but you will first need to do a little task for me.

the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.player: How did I know it wouldn't be that simple for your vote?

the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.speaker: Sigmund The Merchant
the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.text: Calm yourself outerlander. It is but a small task really... I simply require a flower.

the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.speaker: Sigmund The Merchant
the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.text: The catch? Well... it is not just any flower. Someone in this town has an extremely rare flower from a far off land that they picked up on their travels.

the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.speaker: Sigmund The Merchant
the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.text: I would like you to demonstrate your merchanting skills to me, by persuading them to part with it, and then give it to me for my vote.

the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.player: Well... I guess that doesn't sound too hard...

the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.speaker: Sigmund The Merchant
the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.text: Excellent! You will obtain this rare flower for me then?

steps.player: Okay. I don't think this will be too difficult. Any suggestions on where to start looking for this flower?

steps.speaker: Sigmund The Merchant
steps.text: Ah, well outerlander, if I knew where to start looking I would simply do it myself!

steps.player: No help at ALL?

steps.speaker: Sigmund The Merchant
steps.text: We are a very insular clan, so I would not expect you to have to leave this town to find whatever you need.

steps.player: You know what? No. This all sounds like a lot of hassle to me, and frankly I just can't be bothered with it right now.
I'll go get someone else to vote for me.

steps.speaker: Sigmund The Merchant
steps.text: As you wish outerlander. If you change your mind, come and see me again; I am very interested in getting my hands on that flower.

the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.text: If the player attempts to give Sigmund other types of flowers:

steps.text: Nothing interesting happens.

the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.speaker: Sigmund The Merchant
the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.text: So... how goes it outerlander? Did you manage to obtain my flower for me yet? Or do you lack the necessary merchanting skills?

the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.player: I'm still working on it... Do you have any suggestion where to start looking for it?

the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.speaker: Sigmund The Merchant
the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.text: I suggest you ask around the other Fremennik in the town. A good merchant will find exactly what their customer needs somewhere.

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find a rare flower from across the sea, do you?

steps.speaker: Askeladden
steps.text: Nope, sorry buddy!

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find a rare flower from across the sea, do you?

steps.speaker: Thora the Barkeep
steps.text: I wouldn't know about that, outerlander.

the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.text: Greetings again outerlander! How goes your attempts to gain votes with the council of elders?

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find a rare flower from across the sea, do you?

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: Not really my affair, outerlander.

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find a rare flower from across the sea, do you?

steps.speaker: Olaf the Bard
steps.text: I'm sorry, no I don't.

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find a rare flower from across the sea, do you?

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: Not in the slightest.

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find a rare flower from across the sea, do you?

steps.speaker: Skulgrimen
steps.text: I never saw anything like that in my store before.

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find a rare flower from across the sea, do you?

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: I never saw anything like that in my store before.

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find a rare flower from across the sea, do you?

steps.speaker: Peer the Seer
steps.text: I'm afraid not, outerlander.

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find a rare flower from across the sea, do you?

steps.speaker: Yrsa
steps.text: No... sorry, I don't.

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find a rare flower from across the sea, do you?

steps.speaker: Manni the Reveller
steps.text: I have not the first idea about that.

steps.speaker: Sigli the Huntsman
steps.text: Greetings outerlander.

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find a rare flower from across the sea, do you?

steps.speaker: Sigli the Huntsman
steps.text: No idea at all outerlander.

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find a rare flower from across the sea, do you?

steps.speaker: Sailor
steps.text: Ah! Even the outerlanders have heard of my mysterious flower! I found it in a country far far away from here!

steps.player: Can I buy it from you?

steps.speaker: Sailor
steps.text: I'm afraid not, outerlander. There is a woman in this village whose heart I seek to capture, and I think giving her this strange flower might be my best bet with her.

steps.player: Maybe you could let me have the flower and do something else to impress her?

steps.speaker: Sailor
steps.text: Hmm... that is not a totally stupid idea outerlander. I know she is a lover of music, and a romantic ballad might be just the thing with which to woo her.

steps.speaker: Sailor
steps.text: Unfortunately I don't have a musical bone in my entire body, so someone else will have to write it for me.

steps.player: So if I can find someone to write you a romantic ballad, you will give me your flower?

steps.speaker: Sailor
steps.text: That sounds like a fair deal to me, outerlander.

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find a love ballad, do you?

steps.speaker: Olaf the Bard
steps.text: Well, as official Fremennik bard, it falls within my remit to compose all music for the tribe. I am fully versed in all the various types of romantic music.

steps.player: Great! Can you write me one then?

steps.speaker: Olaf the Bard
steps.text: Well... normally I would be thrilled at the chance to show my skill as a poet in composing a seductively romantic ballad...

steps.player: let me guess; here comes the 'but'.

steps.speaker: Olaf the Bard
steps.text: ...but unfortunately I cannot concentrate fully upon my work recently.

steps.player: Why is that then?

steps.speaker: Olaf the Bard
steps.text: It is these old worn out shoes of mine... As a bard I am expected to wander the lands, singing of the glorious battles of our warriors.

steps.speaker: Olaf the Bard
steps.text: If you can find me a pair of sturdy boots to replace these old worn out ones of mine, I will be happy to spend the time on composing you a romantic ballad.

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find some custom sturdy boots, do you?

steps.speaker: Yrsa
steps.text: Well, I don't usually have many shoes in stock here in my little clothes shop... I will be able to make you up a pair if you are really desperate though?

steps.player: They're not for me... I need them for Olaf.

steps.speaker: Yrsa
steps.text: Oh, that foolish bard... Why didn't he just ask me to make him some? It is his stupid pride, I believe!

steps.speaker: Yrsa
steps.text: I will tell you what I will do outerlander; I know that you must have the ear of the chieftain for him to consider you as worthy of becoming a Fremennik by trial.

steps.speaker: Yrsa
steps.text: I will make you a pair of sturdy boots for Olaf if you will persuade him to reduce the sales tax placed upon all Fremennik shopkeepers. It does nothing but hurt my business now.

steps.player: Okay, I will see what I can do.
I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find a guarantee of a reduction on sales taxes, do you?

steps.speaker: Yrsa
steps.text: Yes I do outerlander. Only the Chieftain may permit such a thing. Talk to him.

the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.text: Greetings again outerlander! How goes your attempts to gain votes with the council of elders?

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find a guarantee of a reduction on sales taxes, do you?

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: A reduction on sales taxes? Why, I am the only one in the Fremennik who may authorise such a thing. What does an outerlander want with that?

steps.player: Actually, it's not for me. I need to get it as part of my trials.

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: Hmmm. Interesting. Your trials seem to be very different to those I took as a young lad. Well, I am not adverse in principle to giving a slight tax break to our shops.

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: There will of course be a shortfall in the tribe's income, that will need to be made up for elsewhere, however.

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: How about this. For many years Sigli has been the only one in the tribe who knows the locations of the best hunting grounds where game is easiest to catch.

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: If you can persuade him to let the entire tribe know these hunting grounds, then we can increase productivity within the tribe, and any shortfall caused

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: by lowering sales taxes will be covered. I think this is a more than fair arrangement to make, don't you?

steps.player: Yeah, that sounds very fair.

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: Speak to Sigli then, and you may have my promise to reduce our sales taxes. And best of luck with the rest of your trials.

steps.speaker: Sigli the Huntsman
steps.text: Greetings outerlander.

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find a map to unspoiled hunting grounds, do you?

steps.speaker: Sigli the Huntsman
steps.text: Well, of course I do. I wouldn't be much of a huntsman if I didn't know where to find my prey now, would I outerlander?

steps.player: No, I guess not. So can I have it?

steps.speaker: Sigli the Huntsman
steps.text: Directions to my hunting grounds could mean the end of my livelihood. The only way I would be prepared to give them up would be...

steps.player: What? Power? Money? Women? Wine?

steps.speaker: Sigli the Huntsman
steps.text: ...a new string for my hunting bow. Not just any bowstring; I need a custom bowstring, balanced for my bow precisely to keep my hunt competitive.

steps.speaker: Sigli the Huntsman
steps.text: Only in this way would I allow the knowledge of my hunting grounds to be passed on to strangers.

steps.player: So where would I get that?

steps.speaker: Sigli the Huntsman
steps.text: I have no idea. But then again, I'm happy with my old bowstring and being the only person who knows where my hunting ground is.

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find a finely balanced custom bowstring, do you?

steps.speaker: Askeladden
steps.text: Nope, sorry buddy!

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find a finely balanced custom bowstring, do you?

steps.speaker: Olaf the Bard
steps.text: I'm sorry, no I don't.

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find a finely balanced custom bowstring, do you?

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: Not in the slightest.

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find a finely balanced custom bowstring, do you?

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: I never saw anything like that in my store before.

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find a finely balanced custom bowstring, do you?

steps.speaker: Sailor
steps.text: Not really my affair, outerlander.

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find a finely balanced custom bowstring, do you?

steps.speaker: Yrsa
steps.text: No... sorry, I don't.

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find a finely balanced custom bowstring, do you?

steps.speaker: Peer the Seer
steps.text: I'm afraid not, outerlander.

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find a finely balanced custom bowstring, do you?

steps.speaker: Manni the Reveller
steps.text: I have not the first idea about that.

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find a finely balanced custom bowstring, do you?

steps.speaker: Skulgrimen
steps.text: Aye, I have a few in stock. What would an outerlander be wanting with equipment like that?

steps.player: It's for Sigli. It needs to be weighted precisely to suit his hunting bow.

steps.speaker: Skulgrimen
steps.text: For Sigli eh? Well, I made his bow in the first place, so I'll be able to select the right string for you... just one small problem.

steps.player: What's that?

steps.speaker: Skulgrimen
steps.text: This string you'll be wanting... Very rare. Take a lot of time to recreate. Not sure you have the cash for it.

steps.player: Then maybe you'll accept something else...?

steps.speaker: Skulgrimen
steps.text: Heh. Good thinking outerlander. Well, it's true, there is more to life than just making money. Making weapons is good money, but it's not why I do it.

steps.speaker: Skulgrimen
steps.text: I'll tell you what. I heard a rumour that one of the fishermen down by the docks caught some weird looking fish as they were fishing the other day.

steps.speaker: Skulgrimen
steps.text: From what I hear this fish is unique. Nobody's ever seen its like before. This intrigues me. I'd like to have it for myself. Make a good trophy.

steps.speaker: Skulgrimen
steps.text: You get me that fish, I give you the bowstring. What do you say? We got a deal?

steps.player: Sounds good to me.
I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find an exotic and extremely rare fish, do you?

steps.speaker: Skulgrimen
steps.text: What? There's another one?

steps.player: Er... no, it's the one for you that I'm looking for...

steps.speaker: Skulgrimen
steps.text: Ah. I see. I already told you. Some guy down by the docks was bragging. Best ask there, I reckon.

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find an exotic and extremely rare fish, do you?

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: Ah, so even outerlanders have heard of my amazing catch the other day!

steps.player: You have it? Can I trade you something for it?

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: As exotic looking as it is, it is bad eating. I will happily trade it if you can find me the secret map of the best fishing spots that the navigator has hidden away.

steps.player: Is that all?

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: Indeed it is, outerlander. The only reason I sit out here in the cold all day long is so I don't have to pay his outrageous prices.

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: By getting me his copy of that map, I will finally be self sufficient. I might even make a profit!

steps.player: I'll see what I can do.
I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find a map of deep sea fishing spots do you?

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: You should pay attention when I speak! I already told you, that rip off navigator has it, and I want it!

steps.speaker: Swensen the Navigator
steps.text: Greetings outerlander.

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find a map of deep sea fishing spots do you?

steps.speaker: Swensen the Navigator
steps.text: Hmmm? Why of course! As the navigator for the Fremennik I keep all of our maps secure right here.

steps.player: Great! Can I have it?

steps.speaker: Swensen the Navigator
steps.text: Have it? Just like that? I think not outerlander. This map shows all of the prime fishing locations nearby.

steps.speaker: Swensen the Navigator
steps.text: It is very valuable to our clan. I am afraid I can not just give it away.

steps.player: Perhaps I can trade you something for it?

steps.speaker: Swensen the Navigator
steps.text: A trade? For a map of the best fishing spots in a hundred leagues? I will trade it for no less than a weather forecast from our Seer.

steps.speaker: Swensen the Navigator
steps.text: As a navigator, the weather is extremely important for plotting the best course. Unfortunately the Seer is always too busy to help me with a forecast.

steps.player: Where could I get a weather forecast from then?

steps.speaker: Swensen the Navigator
steps.text: I just told you: from the Seer. You will need to persuade him to take the time to make a forecast somehow.

steps.speaker: Swensen the Navigator
steps.text: Greetings outerlander.

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find a weather forecast from the Fremennik Seer do you?

steps.speaker: Swensen the Navigator
steps.text: Uh... from the Seer perhaps?

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find a weather forecast from the Fremennik Seer do you?

steps.speaker: Peer the Seer
steps.text: Er.... Yes, because I AM the Fremennik Seer.

steps.player: Can I have a weather forecast then please?

steps.speaker: Peer the Seer
steps.text: You require a divination of the weather? This is a simple matter for me, but I will require something in return from you for this small service.

steps.player: I knew you were going to say that...

steps.speaker: Peer the Seer
steps.text: Do not fret, outerlander; it is a fairly simple matter. I require a bodyguard for protection. Find someone willing to offer me this service.

steps.player: That's all?

steps.speaker: Peer the Seer
steps.text: That is all.

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find a brave and powerful warrior to act as a bodyguard?

steps.speaker: Peer the Seer
steps.text: If I did, then I would simply have asked them myself now, wouldn't I, outerlander?

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find a brave and powerful warrior to act as a bodyguard?

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: Know you not who I am outerlander? There are none more brave or powerful than me amongst all the Fremennik!

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: However... The role of bodyguard is below me, as a noble warrior. You might as well ask me to babysit the children!

steps.player: Is there no way you would do this for me?

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: There is but one way outerlander. Since I was steeled in battle, I have dreamt of earning my place at the Champions Table in the Long Hall.

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: It is a tradition amongst us that the bravest and strongest are honoured with a table of champions to drink and feast all that they can in our Long Hall.

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: Unfortunately, there are only a fixed number of places available at the table, and these places were all filled many moons ago by others.

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: Although my worthiness is undeniable, the only way I may take my place is if one of those already there die, or give up their place to me voluntarily.

steps.player: So you want me to go kill one of them off for you? Make it look like an accident?

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: WHAT? No, no, not at all! I am shocked you would suggest such a thing!

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: If you can persuade one of the Revellers to give up their Champions' Token to you so that I might take their place, you may have my contract as a bodyguard.

steps.player: Okay, I'll see what I can do.
I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find a Champions' Token?

steps.speaker: Thorvald
steps.text: If you can persuade one of the Revellers to give up their Champions' Token to you so that I might take their place, you may have my contract as a bodyguard.

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find a token to allow a seat at the champions table, do you?

steps.speaker: Manni the Reveller
steps.text: As a matter of fact, I do. I have one right here. I earnt my place here at the longhall for surviving over 5000 battles and raiding parties.

steps.speaker: Manni the Reveller
steps.text: Due to my contribution to the tribe, I am now permitted to spend my days here in the longhall listening to the epic tales of the bard, and drinking beer.

steps.player: Cool. That sounds pretty sweet! So I guess you don't want to give it away?

steps.speaker: Manni the Reveller
steps.text: I think it sounds better than it actually is outerlander. I miss my glory days of combat on the battlefield. And to tell you the truth, the beer here isn't great, and the bards' music is lousy.

steps.speaker: Manni the Reveller
steps.text: I would happily give up my token if it were not for the one thing that keeps me here. Our barkeep is one of the best in the world, and has worked in taverns across the land.

steps.speaker: Manni the Reveller
steps.text: When she was younger, she experimented a lot with her drinks, and invented a cocktail so alcoholic and tasty that it has become something of a legend to all who enjoy a drink.

steps.speaker: Manni the Reveller
steps.text: Unfortunately, she decided that cocktails were not a suitable drink for Fremennik warriors, and vowed to never again make it.

steps.speaker: Manni the Reveller
steps.text: I have been here every day since she returned, hoping that someday she might change her mind and I might try this legendary cocktail for myself. Alas, it has never come to pass...

steps.speaker: Manni the Reveller
steps.text: If you can persuade her to make me her legendary cocktail, I will be happy to never let another drop of alcohol pass my lips, and will give you my champions token.

steps.player: That's all?

steps.speaker: Manni the Reveller
steps.text: That's all.

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find the longhall barkeeps' legendary cocktail, do you?

steps.speaker: Manni the Reveller
steps.text: Uh... yes, the longhall barkeep has it. So could you get me my drink now please?

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find the longhall barkeeps' legendary cocktail, do you?

steps.speaker: Thora the Barkeep
steps.text: How did you hear about that?!?!?

steps.speaker: Thora the Barkeep
steps.text: I didn't think anybody knew about that... Well, it is true that in my younger years as a barkeep, I wandered the lands trying various alcoholic delicacies.

steps.speaker: Thora the Barkeep
steps.text: Did you ever realise just how many different types of alcohol there are here in Gielinor? Lots!

steps.speaker: Thora the Barkeep
steps.text: Well, anyway, I used a fusion of various drinks from all around the world to create the greatest cocktail ever made!

steps.speaker: Thora the Barkeep
steps.text: Of course, when my wanderlust was gone, and I returned back to Rellekka to serve as barkeep here, I gave all that up.

steps.player: But you still remember how to make it, right?

steps.speaker: Thora the Barkeep
steps.text: Of course.

steps.player: And you have all the ingredients here? I don't need to go chasing round the world for obscure ingredients to make it?

steps.speaker: Thora the Barkeep
steps.text: No, I have them all here. Why?

steps.player: Can you make me your legendary cocktail then?

steps.speaker: Thora the Barkeep
steps.text: I would rather not; it is a reminder of a life I left behind when I came back.

steps.player: Any way I could change your mind?

steps.speaker: Thora the Barkeep
steps.text: You need this to become a Fremennik, right? Well, you seem okay for an outerlander, it would be a shame to see you fail. You know Askeladden?

steps.player: That kid outside? Sure.

steps.speaker: Thora the Barkeep
steps.text: He is nothing but a pest. He keeps sneaking in and stealing beer. I shudder to think what he will be like when he has passed his trial of manhood,

steps.speaker: Thora the Barkeep
steps.text: and is allowed in here legitimately. If you can get him to sign a contract promising that he will NEVER EVER EVER darken my doorway here again, you get the drink.

steps.player: Any idea how I can get him to do that?

steps.speaker: Thora the Barkeep
steps.text: Knowing that little horror, he'll probably be willing to in exchange for some cash. You should go ask him yourself though.

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find a written promise from Askeladden to stay out of the Longhall?

steps.speaker: Thora the Barkeep
steps.text: Well, as I say, you should talk to him about that. Knowing the little runt as I do though He'll probably do it for the cash.

steps.player: I don't suppose you have any idea where I could find a written promise from Askeladden to stay out of the Longhall?

steps.speaker: Askeladden
steps.text: What? I can't believe she asked you to get a written promise from me to stay out!

steps.player: Yup, she really did.

steps.speaker: Askeladden
steps.text: Awwwwwww.... but the longhall is just SO MUCH FUN! I'd live there if I could! I suppose you really need that promise to help become a Fremennik, huh?

steps.player: Yeah, I really do...

steps.speaker: Askeladden
steps.text: Well I'll tell you what buddy; As it's you, I'll give you that written promise. All I ask in return for it is a measly 5000 gold. What do you say?

steps.player: That's all you want in return? Sure thing. Here you go.

steps.text: If the player does not have 5,000 gp:

steps.player: ...how embarrassing. I appear to be short...

steps.speaker: Askeladden
steps.text: Trying to scam me, huh buddy? Well it won't work! You come back with the cash, or don't come back at all!
If the player has 5,000 gp:
If the player's inventory is full:
Your inventory is too full to accept the written promise.
If the player has inventory space:
a Promissory note

steps.speaker: Askeladden
steps.text: Done, and done. Let me know if you got any more cash burning a hole in your pocket I can relieve you of, buddy.

steps.player: I don't think so... That's really quite a lot of money...

steps.speaker: Askeladden
steps.text: Hey, suit yourself buddy. You change your mind, the bank of Askeladden is open for deposits 24 hours a day! Eh-heh-heh-heh-heh.

steps.player: I thought you really liked the long hall?

steps.speaker: Askeladden
steps.text: I do!

steps.player: Then why did you sign this guarantee that you will never enter it again?

steps.speaker: Askeladden
steps.text: Aha! It is because I am cunning! That guarantee says that Askeladden will never enter the longhall again! But when I have completed my Fremennik trials,

steps.speaker: Askeladden
steps.text: and passed my trial of manhood, I will be given a new name, as is our custom, and will therefore not be Askeladden anymore! That guarantee isn't worth the paper it's written on!!

steps.speaker: Askeladden
steps.text: You didn't think I would give up going to the longhall for only 5000 did you?

steps.player: Knowing you, I guess I didn't.
Hi! Can I please have one of your legendary cocktails now?

steps.speaker: Thora the Barkeep
steps.text: What?!?! I can't believe you... Let me look at that... Askeladden would NEVER... Gosh. It looks legitimate.

steps.speaker: Thora the Barkeep
steps.text: Here you go, on the house! You have made my life SO much easier! Knowing that little monster won't be bugging me in here all the time anymore!
a legendary cocktail

steps.speaker: Thora the Barkeep
steps.text: That little weasel will have to abide by this written promise that Askeladden can never ever enter the Longhall again! He can't get round this one!

steps.player: Uh... yeah... yeah, you probably won't see someone called Askeladden coming in here...
Thanks for making me this cocktail. Why don't you make them anymore normally?

steps.speaker: Thora the Barkeep
steps.text: Ah... when I gave up my travels across the world many years back, to return to my expected role as longhall barkeep, as my mother, and her mother, were before me,

steps.speaker: Thora the Barkeep
steps.text: I gave up a lot of the freedom I had found in the outside world. I know it is our custom to shun outerlanders and their ways, but I didn't find them as bad as the stories say.

steps.speaker: Thora the Barkeep
steps.text: Sometimes I feel as though we Fremennik live in a prison that we have constructed for ourselves, and that WE are the outerlanders, out here on the edge of the world...

steps.speaker: Thora the Barkeep
steps.text: I'm sorry, I think it is part of the job of Longhall barkeep to get philosophical about things ocassionally. I wish you all the best of luck with your trials, outerlander.

steps.speaker: Thora the Barkeep
steps.text: When you have finished, perhaps you will come back here, and we can share a drink over tales of the outside world?

steps.player: Thanks, I'd like that.
Hey. I got your cocktail for you.

steps.speaker: Manni the Reveller
steps.text: ...It is true! The legendary cocktail! I have waited for this day ever since I first started drinking!

steps.speaker: Manni the Reveller
steps.text: Here outerlander, you may take my token. I will happily give up my place at the longhalls table of champions just for a taste of this exquisite beverage!
a champions token

steps.player: It's just a drink...

steps.speaker: Manni the Reveller
steps.text: No, it is an artform. A drink such as this should be appreciated, and admired. It is like a fine painting, or a tasteful sculpture.

steps.speaker: Manni the Reveller
steps.text: If what I hear is true, then all other drinks become like unpalatable water in comparison to this!

steps.player: I guess you're happy with the trade then!
So it doesn't bother you at all that you just gave up your place here for one drink?

steps.speaker: Manni the Reveller
steps.text: Ah, but it was not just any drink... It was the finest cocktail ever created! Now that I have tasted it, I need never drink again, for my tastebuds will never be so excited!

steps.player: So it was nice?

steps.speaker: Manni the Reveller
steps.text: It was... exquisite!

steps.player: What did it taste of, then?

steps.speaker: Manni the Reveller
steps.text: Mostly tomato juice.

steps.player: I would like your contract to offer your services as a bodyguard.

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: Oh you would, would you outerlander? I have already told you, I will not demean myself with such a baby sitting job until I can sit in the Longhall with pride.

steps.player: It's a good thing I have the Champions' Token right here then, isn't it?

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: Ah... well this is a different matter. With that token I can claim my rightful place as a champion in the Long hall!

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: Here outerlander, I can suffer the indignity of playing babysitter if it means that I can then revel with my warrior equals in the Long Hall afterwards!

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: Here outerlander, take this contract; I will fulfill it to my utmost.
a warriors' contract

steps.player: You didn't take much persuading to 'lower' yourself to a bodyguard.

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: You misunderstand, outerlander. Normally I will only battle for a noble cause, but have never been recognised as a true champion here.

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: With this Champion's token, I can stand alongside my warrior brethren in the Long Hall, and revel in the glories of past victories together!

steps.player: Can I have a weather forecast now please?

steps.speaker: Peer the Seer
steps.text: I have already told you outerlander; You may have a reading from me when I have a signed contract from a warrior guaranteeing my protection.

steps.player: Yeah, I know; I have one right here from Thorvald.

steps.speaker: Peer the Seer
steps.text: You have not only persuaded one of the Fremennik to act as a servant to me, but you have enlisted the aid of mighty Thorvald himself???

steps.speaker: Peer the Seer
steps.text: You may take this forecast with my blessing outerlander. You have offered me the greatest security I can imagine.
a weather forecast

steps.player: So, about this forecast...

steps.speaker: Peer the Seer
steps.text: Yes, outerlander?

steps.player: I still don't know why you didn't just let me have one anyway in the first place. Surely it means nothing to you?

steps.speaker: Peer the Seer
steps.text: That is not true, outerlander. Although I see glimpses of the future all of the time, using my powers brings the attention of the gods to me.

steps.speaker: Peer the Seer
steps.text: Some of the gods are spiteful and cruel, and I fear if I use my powers too much then I will meet with unpredictable accidents. This is why I needed protection.

steps.player: Okay... I... think I understand...
I would like your map of fishing spots.

steps.speaker: Swensen the Navigator
steps.text: I have already told you outerlander; I will not exchange it for anything other than a divination on the weather from our seer himself!

steps.player: What, like this one I have here?

steps.speaker: Swensen the Navigator
steps.text: W-what...? I don't believe it! How did you...? I suppose it doesn't matter, you have my gratitude outerlander!

steps.speaker: Swensen the Navigator
steps.text: With this forecast I will be able to plan a safe course for our next raiding expedition!

steps.speaker: Swensen the Navigator
steps.text: Here, outerlander; you may take my map of local fishing patterns with my gratitude!
a sea fishing map

steps.player: If this map of fishing spots is so valuable, why did you give it away to me so easily?

steps.speaker: Swensen the Navigator
steps.text: Hmmm? Well, firstly it will be of value to our entire clan, so I have lost nothing from giving it to you.

steps.speaker: Swensen the Navigator
steps.text: The other reason is of course that I have already memorised it, so I can make myself another copy whenever I want!

steps.player: Here. I got you your map.

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: Great work outerlander! With this, I can finally catch enough fish to make an honest living from it! Here, have the stupid rare fish.
an unusual fish

steps.player: I don't see what's so special about this so called rare fish.

steps.speaker: Fisherman
steps.text: Me neither, outerlander. That is why I gave it to you.

steps.player: Hi there. I got your fish, so can I have that bowstring for Sigli now?

steps.speaker: Skulgrimen
steps.text: Ohh... That's a nice fish. Very pleased. Here. Take the bowstring. You fulfilled agreement. only fair I do same. Good work outerlander.
a custom bow string

steps.player: Thanks!
So about this bowstring... was it hard to make or something?

steps.speaker: Skulgrimen
steps.text: Not hard. Just a trick to it. Takes skill to learn, but when learnt, easy. Sigli will be happy. Finest bowstring on continent. Will suit his needs perfectly.

steps.speaker: Sigli the Huntsman
steps.text: Greetings outerlander.

steps.player: Here. I have your bowstring. Give me your map to the hunting grounds.

steps.speaker: Sigli the Huntsman
steps.text: Well met, outerlander. I see some hunting potential within you. Here, take my map, I was getting too dependent on it for my skill anyway.
a tracking map

steps.player: So you really don't mind giving this away to me?

steps.speaker: Sigli the Huntsman
steps.text: No outerlander... it is hard to explain. That map makes my role as huntsman too easy. I fear my skills are becoming dulled. Now I must track my prey once more.

steps.speaker: Sigli the Huntsman
steps.text: To begin again from scratch... I feel this may keep me sharp.

the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.text: Greetings again outerlander! How goes your attempts to gain votes with the council of elders?

steps.player: I got Sigli's hunting map for you.

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: Excellent work outerlander! And so quickly, too! Here, you may take my financial report promising reduced sales taxes on all goods.
a fiscal statement

steps.player: So cutting sales tax isn't going to ruin your economy here or anything?

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: Not at all outerlander; now that we have Sigli's map we can increase the amount of hunts we run, and make up any shortfall that way.

steps.player: Hello. Can I have those boots now? Here is a written statement from Brundt outlining future tax burdens upon Fremennik merchants and shopkeepers for the year.

steps.speaker: Yrsa
steps.text: Certainly! Let me have a look at what he has written here, just give me a moment...
a pair of Sturdy boots

steps.speaker: Yrsa
steps.text: Yes, that all appears in order. Tell Olaf to come to me next time for shoes!

steps.player: Hey, these shoes look pretty comfy. Think you could make me a pair like them?

steps.speaker: Yrsa
steps.text: Maybe if you pass your trial and become a full fledged member of the Fremennik...

steps.player: Hello Olaf. Do you have a beautiful love song written for me?

steps.speaker: Olaf the Bard
steps.text: That depends outerlander... Do you have some new boots for me? My feet get so tired roaming the land...

steps.player: As a matter of fact - I do!

steps.text: a Fremennik ballad

steps.speaker: Olaf the Bard
steps.text: Oh! Superb! Those are great! They're just what I was looking for! Here, take this song with my compliments! It is one of my finest works yet!

steps.player: So you think this song is pretty good then?

steps.speaker: Olaf the Bard
steps.text: Ahhh.... outerlander... it is the most beautiful romantic ballad I have ever been inspired to write...

steps.speaker: Olaf the Bard
steps.text: Only a woman with a heart of icy stone could fail to be moved by its beauty!

steps.player: Thanks! That sounds perfect!

the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.text: If the player attempts to use the ballad on the Ice Queen:

steps.text: Nothing interesting happens.

steps.player: You'll be glad to know I have had a love song written just for you by Olaf. So can I have that flower of yours now?

steps.speaker: Sailor
steps.text: Oh. It's by Olaf? Hmm. Well, a deal's a deal. I just hope it's better than the usual rubbish he comes up with, or my chances are worse than ever.
an exotic flower

steps.player: so tell me... who is this woman that you are trying to impress anyway?

steps.speaker: Sailor
steps.text: It's Thora, the longhall barkeep. Please don't tell her though. She's not like the rest of the Fremennik girls, she has a secret desire to see the world.

steps.speaker: Sailor
steps.text: Being a sailor, I can really relate to that.

the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.speaker: Sigmund The Merchant
the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.text: Incredible! Your merchanting skills might even match my own! I have no choice but to recommend you to the council of elders!

the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.speaker: Sigmund The Merchant
the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.text: Hello again outerlander! I am amazed once more at your apparent skill at merchanting!

the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.player: So I can count on your vote at the council of elders?

the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.speaker: Sigmund The Merchant
the-council-members-sigmund-the-merchant.text: Absolutely, outerlander. Your merchanting skills will be a real boon to the Fremennik.

the-council-members-thorvald-the-warrior.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
the-council-members-thorvald-the-warrior.text: Hello yourself, outerlander. What brings you to dare speak to a mighty Fremennik warrior such as myself?

the-council-members-thorvald-the-warrior.player: Erm... are you a member of the council?

the-council-members-thorvald-the-warrior.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
the-council-members-thorvald-the-warrior.text: The Fremennik council of elders? Why, of course I am. I am recognised as one the clans mightiest warriors. What is it to you outerlander?

the-council-members-thorvald-the-warrior.player: Well... I was wondering if you could vote for me to become a Fremennik.

the-council-members-thorvald-the-warrior.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
the-council-members-thorvald-the-warrior.text: An outerlander wishes to become a Fremennik!?!? Ha! That is priceless!

the-council-members-thorvald-the-warrior.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
the-council-members-thorvald-the-warrior.text: Well, let us say that I am not totally against this concept. As a warrior, I appreciate the value of brave and powerful warriors to our clan,

the-council-members-thorvald-the-warrior.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
the-council-members-thorvald-the-warrior.text: and even though you may be an outerlander, I will not hold this against you if you can prove yourself to be fierce of heart in a combat situation to me.

the-council-members-thorvald-the-warrior.player: So how can I prove that? You want to fight me? Come on then, bring it on! Right here, right now, buddy!

the-council-members-thorvald-the-warrior.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
the-council-members-thorvald-the-warrior.text: Hahahahaha! You certainly show some spirit for an outerlander!

the-council-members-thorvald-the-warrior.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
the-council-members-thorvald-the-warrior.text: But spirit does not always make a good warrior. It takes both skill and spirit to be so. I have a test that I give all Fremenniks on their path to be a member of the clan.

the-council-members-thorvald-the-warrior.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
the-council-members-thorvald-the-warrior.text: My test will challenge both your combat prowess and your bravery equally. Should you pass it you will earn my vote at the council, and more importantly my respect for you as a warrior.

the-council-members-thorvald-the-warrior.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
the-council-members-thorvald-the-warrior.text: So what say you, outerlander? Are you prepared for the battle?

steps.player: Am I prepared? I'll show you what combat's all about, you big sissy barbarian type guy!

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: Hahahahaha! I'm beginning to like you already, outerlander!

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: Then allow me to present you with my challenge; This ladder here will take you to a place of combat. I have placed a special warrior down there to challenge you.

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: Battle him to the death, and you will pass my challenge. If at any point you wish to leave combat, simply climb back up the ladder, to leave that place.

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: If you leave you will of course fail the test. You may retry my test in the future if you fail, but you must stay down there until the death if you wish for my vote at the council.

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: You must defeat him three times to prove that you are worthy. The fourth time that you fight him will be to the death, so do not show cowardice.

steps.player: Is that all? It will be easy!

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: No, there is one more important rule;

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: You may not enter the battleground with any armour or weaponry of any kind.

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: If you need to place your equipment into your bank account, I recommend that you speak to the seer, who knows a spell that will do that for you.

steps.player: No thanks, I'm pretty sure that I can find someone else to vote for me.

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: Hmm, not so brave after all, outerlander? Perhaps it is for the best. I doubt you have what it takes to pass my challenge.

options.text: What do I have to do again?

steps.player: So what do I have to do to earn your vote at the council again?

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: I will not offer my vote to anybody whose bravery in combat I do not trust completely. You must go down that ladder and fight your foe to the death.

steps.player: So, who is my opponent?

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: Ah, a wise question before entering combat. His name is Koschei the deathless. He is something of a mystery, even to us.

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: On one of our regular raiding parties, our longship discovered a man in the frozen waters far north-east of here. We took him aboard our ship, thinking he must be dead.

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: To our amazement he was perfectly healthy, even though he must have been in those deadly icy waters for many weeks.

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: He has no memory of who he is, or how he came to be there, except for his own name: Koschei. We named him 'The Deathless' because he is seemingly unkillable!

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: Any combat technique used against him, he learns instantly! He also apparently can heal himself from any wound at will! When he attacks, his weapon moves like a whirlwind!

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: He can hide his combat level from his opponents at will as well! He is truly a horribly fierce opponent to face! I am only glad that he has chosen to stay here with us!

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: The daylight makes him feel weak, so we have built him his own battleground beneath this building, where he can train his fiercesome skills without being disturbed.

steps.player: But he can't REALLY be unkillable...  ...can he?

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: Some say he cannot die, for he has hidden his heart outside of his body to be kept forever safe in a duck egg.

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: Others say he has been cursed by the gods to wander this land forever, never knowing any peace in his life, but only combat.

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: Some claim that the sword he carries is the source of all his power, and if he should lose it, then exactly one minute later, he will turn back into his true form;

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: A weakened, lame, old man.

steps.player: And what do you believe?

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: I believe you shouldn't look a gift horse in the mouth. He is a fearfully powerful warrior, but more importantly; He is on OUR side, not against us.

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: He is content testing the battle skills of anyone taking their Fremennik trials of manhood, and I am content knowing that should an enemy ever invade our town,

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: while our warriors are out on a raiding party, Koschei will be able to hold off ANY invader long enough for us to make our return.

steps.player: I don't really like fighting that much... Isn't there something else I can do to earn your vote at the council of elders?

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: Yes of course outerlander! If you bring me five raw sardines then I will vote for you instead!

steps.player: REALLY?!?!?

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: HAHAHAHAHAHA! No, of course not! You are stupid, even by outerlander standards!

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: If you want my vote, you must pass my trial. It is as simple as that.

the-council-members-thorvald-the-warrior.text: If the player attempts to use a raw sardine on Thorvald:

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: I was only joking about the raw sardines outerlander.

steps.player: Oh. Really? Oh. So I have to pass your combat trial?

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: Yes.

steps.player: Hello there! Thorvald tells me you can deposit my equipment directly into my bank account for me...?

steps.speaker: Peer the Seer
steps.text: That is correct outerlander, but you will need to go and retrieve your equipment from your bank account yourself, manually.

steps.speaker: Peer the Seer
steps.text: Alas, my spell is not very accurate, so it will deposit everything you have upon you into your bank, not just your armour and weapons.

steps.player: Yes, please deposit my equipment.

steps.text: If the player's bank is full or if the player has unbankable items (e.g. a Lamp or experience tome):

steps.speaker: Peer the Seer
steps.text: I am sorry outerlander, the spell is not working.
If the player's bank is not full:
Peer the seer banks all of the player's contents from their inventory and worn equipment.

steps.speaker: Peer the Seer
steps.text: The task is done. I wish you luck with your test, outerlander.

steps.player: No thanks, I'll just go to the bank and sort my inventory out myself.

the-council-members-peer-the-seer-enteri.text: If the player has any weapons or armour before entering the arena:

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: You may not enter the battleground with any armour or weaponry of any kind.

steps.speaker: Thorvald the Warrior
steps.text: If you need to place your equipment into your bank account, I recommend that you speak to the seer, who knows a spell that will do that for you.

the-council-members-peer-the-seer-enteri.text: If the player does not have any weapons or armour before entering the arena:

steps.text: The person goes into the dungeon.

the-council-members-peer-the-seer-during.text: If the player enters the arena:

steps.text: Explore this battleground and find your foe...

the-council-members-peer-the-seer-during.text: If the player attempts to attack another player's Koschei:

steps.text: This is not your opponent.

the-council-members-peer-the-seer-during.text: If the player fails to defeat Koschei in his third/fourth phase in 10 minutes:

steps.text: You have failed to impress Koschei. He has left in disgust.
You will need to improve your combat skills before challenging him again.

the-council-members-peer-the-seer-during.text: Koschei yells a random dialogue listed below.
At the beginning of the second phase:

steps.speaker: Koschei the deathless
steps.text: It seems you have some idea of combat after all, outerlander! I will not hold back so much this time!

the-council-members-peer-the-seer-during.text: Koschei yells a random dialogue listed below.
At the start of the third phase:

steps.speaker: Koschei the deathless
steps.text: Impressive start... But now we fight for real!

the-council-members-peer-the-seer-during.text: At the start of the fourth phase:

steps.speaker: Koschei the deathless
steps.text: You show some skill at combat... I will hold back no longer! This time you lose your prayer however, and fight like a warrior!
The player's prayer points drop to 0.

the-council-members-peer-the-seer-during.text: If the player attempts to drink a prayer potion:

steps.text: The player's prayer quickly depletes to 0.

the-council-members-peer-the-seer-during.text: If the player is nearly dead at 1 hitpoint:

steps.text: Oh dear you are...
The player performs a similar death animation by kneeling down very slowly.
The player is teleported upstairs to the {{FloorNumber|uk=3}}.
...still alive somehow?

the-council-members-peer-the-seer-during.text: If the player is able to defeat Koschei in his 4th form:

steps.text: Koschei disappears into a mist and the player receives the Fremennik blade.

steps.speaker: Swensen the Navigator
steps.text: Well, I am sorry you feel that way outerlander. I cannot vouch for you until you prove to me you have some skill that will benefit our clan somehow.

steps.speaker: Swensen the Navigator
steps.text: What exactly is a 'lab rat' anyway?

steps.player: Ah, forget it.

the-council-members-swensen-s-trial-talk.player: Man, your maze is pretty tough!

the-council-members-swensen-s-trial-talk.speaker: Swensen the Navigator
the-council-members-swensen-s-trial-talk.text: Hahahaha it is the most complex route I have ever devised! I am truly a genius at navigation! The world will remember my name!

the-council-members-swensen-s-trial-talk.player: Can't I do something else for your vote at the council of elders?

the-council-members-swensen-s-trial-talk.speaker: Swensen the Navigator
the-council-members-swensen-s-trial-talk.text: No, you cannot. It is my maze, or nothing.

the-council-members-swensen-s-trial-ente.text: If the player attempts to enter through any of the trapdoors:

steps.text: You try to open the trapdoor but it won't budge! It looks like the trapdoor can only be opened from the other side.
You try to open the trapdoor but it won't budge!
It looks like the trapdoor can only be opened from the other side.

the-council-members-swensen-s-trial-ente.text: If the player climbs down the ladder:

the-council-members-swensen-s-trial-whil.text: If the player leaves through the escape rope:

steps.text: The player leaves the maze and exits through the southern trapdoor.

steps.speaker: Swensen the Navigator
steps.text: Decided you could not solve my labyrinth after all, did you outerlander? Too tricky for you?

steps.player: Yeah, it is really confusing down there...

steps.speaker: Swensen the Navigator
steps.text: Hahaha! Don't worry outerlander, you are not the first to fail its puzzle!

the-council-members-swensen-s-trial-whil.text: If the player climbs up the stairs in the north-western portal room:

steps.speaker: Swensen the Navigator
steps.text: Outerlander! You have finished my maze! I am genuinely impressed!

steps.player: So does that mean I can rely on your vote at the council of elders to allow me into your village?

steps.speaker: Swensen the Navigator
steps.text: Of course outerlander! I am nothing if not a man of my word!

steps.player: Thanks!

the-council-members-swensen-s-trial-talk.speaker: Swensen the Navigator
the-council-members-swensen-s-trial-talk.text: Greetings again outerlander! I must say, I am still impressed with the way you moved through my maze!

the-council-members-swensen-s-trial-talk.player: Thanks. So I can rely on your vote in my favour at the council of elders?

the-council-members-swensen-s-trial-talk.speaker: Swensen the Navigator
the-council-members-swensen-s-trial-talk.text: Absolutely! You will be an asset to the clan!
If the player attempts to climb down into the maze again:

steps.player: No way am I doing that maze again!

the-council-members-talking-to-brundt.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
the-council-members-talking-to-brundt.text: Greetings again outerlander! How goes your attempts to gain votes with the council of elders?
If the player has not gotten only one vote:

steps.player: I only have 1 vote so far.

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: Hmmm... well that is certainly a good start I would say. Keep up the good work!

the-council-members-talking-to-brundt.text: If the player has gotten 2-6 votes:

steps.player: I only have [2-6] votes so far.

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: Hmmm... you are doing very well so far, outerlander. Keep up the good work!

the-council-members-talking-to-brundt.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
the-council-members-talking-to-brundt.text: Remember: You need to get at least seven council votes to be accepted as a member of the Fremennik.

the-council-members-talking-to-brundt.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
the-council-members-talking-to-brundt.text: If you need any help with your trials, I suggest you speak to Askeladden. He is currently doing his own trials of manhood to become a true Fremennik.
If the player has gotten all 7 votes:

steps.player: I have seven members of the council prepared to vote in my favour now!

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: I know outerlander, for I have been closely monitoring your progress so far!

steps.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
steps.text: Then let us put the formality aside, and let me personally welcome you into the Fremennik! May you bring us honour!
Congratulations, you've completed a quest: The Fremennik Trials

post-quest-dialogue.speaker: Brundt the Chieftain
post-quest-dialogue.text: From this day onward, you are outerlander no more! In honour of your acceptance into the Fremennik You gain a new name to be known as. You will now be called [Fremennik name].

WL61gt.player: Forget it! This all sounds like way too much work for a stupid vote at a meeting! I'll find someone else instead.
